summary: Modular monolith: Next.js (web) + React Native (Expo) (Android) on Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript) with Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 — Central India (Pune), hosted on Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) — Central India (Pune), at an estimated $84-457/month. Review the warnings: some inputs conflict or carry risk.

frontend.justification: Web: Next.js — Rich interactive app screens; team already writes javascript, typescript for the UI; server-rendered/static HTML that search engines index; good fast delivery (priority 5/5); good low running cost (priority 4/5). Mobile: React Native (Expo) — Team already writes javascript, typescript for the mobile app; shares TypeScript code and skills with the web app; good fast delivery (priority 5/5); good low running cost (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Next.js is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market); same React component model as a React Native mobile app (project.platforms). Overall 4.1 points behind. Known limit of Nuxt: needs a Node server runtime for SSR.

Next.js is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market); rich interactive app screens (project.type). Overall 5.2 points behind. Known limit of SvelteKit: smaller hiring pool than React.

Weaker performance (priority 3/5) (priorities.performance). React Native (Expo) is stronger on: good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 2.8 points behind. Known limit of Ionic Capacitor: WebView performance on low-end devices.

Team lists javascript, python, typescript but this needs kotlin/java (team.languages). React Native (Expo) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 18.0 points behind. Known limit of Kotlin + Jetpack Compose: android only; iOS needs a second codebase.

tradeoffs: Server runtime needed for SSR; more moving parts than a static site
JS runtime overhead on very low-end phones
frontend.contrast: Next.js (web) + React Native (Expo) (Android) rather than Nuxt (Vue SSR/SSG). Next.js is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market); same React component model as a React Native mobile app (project.platforms). Trade-off accepted: Server runtime needed for SSR; more moving parts than a static site.

backend.justification: Team already writes javascript, typescript for the API; native WebSocket support; one language (TypeScript/JavaScript) across clients and server; good low running cost (priority 4/5); good fast delivery (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript) is stronger on: native WebSocket support (requirements.realtime); good performance (priority 3/5) (priorities.performance). Overall 0.8 points behind. Known limit of Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS: WebSockets need Django Channels.

Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript) is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 3/5) (priorities.maintainability); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 3.0 points behind. Known limit of Node.js 24 LTS + Express 5: little structure; large codebases need discipline.

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: low
confidence.basis: stability 0.63 (sensitive) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 0.8 over the runner-up (near-tie).

backend.contrast: Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript) rather than Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS. Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript) is stronger on: native WebSocket support (requirements.realtime); good performance (priority 3/5) (priorities.performance). Trade-off accepted: More boilerplate than Express.

database.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 — Central India (Pune)
database.justification: Strict ACID transactions for bookings and payments; built-in full-text search avoids a separate search service; good low running cost (priority 4/5); good fast delivery (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 4/5) (priorities.cost); good maintainability (priority 3/5) (priorities.maintainability). Overall 6.0 points behind. Known limit of Supabase Postgres: free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity; production needs Pro.

Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 4/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 6.4 points behind. Known limit of Azure SQL Database: licence cost outside Azure SQL; Windows-centric tooling.

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

hosting.choice: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) — Central India (Pune)
hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> Central India (Pune)). Fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; good fast delivery (priority 5/5); good low running cost (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market); good maintainability (priority 3/5) (priorities.maintainability). Overall 1.6 points behind. Known limit of Google Cloud Run: cold starts unless min instances are paid for.

Operations burden 2/5 with no dedicated DevOps person (team.has_devops). Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 10.2 points behind. Known limit of Azure Container Apps: more moving parts than App Service for a single web app.
Excluded: no INDIA region for application data (infrastructure.data_residency).

supporting.justification: phone_otp for Indian users: an Indian SMS provider with DLT-registered templates is the cheapest reliable OTP route (about Rs 0.20 per SMS); the backend stores users and refresh tokens in the in-region database.

alternatives.why_not: stores identity data in Google's global auth service, conflicting with India residency
about $0.05 per verification plus SMS, far above Indian SMS rates

tradeoffs: DLT registration of sender ID/template before launch
OTP needs network at login; sessions must stay valid offline

supporting.justification: Uploads (images, documents) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: bloats backups and costs more per GB
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside AZURE

supporting.justification: At ~30,000 users the primary database's built-in full-text search is enough; no extra service to run or pay for.

alternatives.why_not: a separate cluster to operate before the data size needs it

tradeoffs: Typo tolerance and ranking are basic; move to a search engine if relevance becomes a product feature

supporting.justification: Live updates and chat over WebSockets from the same backend, so authorisation and data stay in one place.

alternatives.why_not: managed fan-out, but an extra vendor and per-connection cost
wastes requests and adds latency

supporting.choice: Razorpay (UPI, cards, netbanking) — Route/RazorpayX Payouts to pay service providers
supporting.justification: Hosted checkout keeps card data off your servers, which can qualify for PCI DSS SAQ A (your acquirer confirms; protect the checkout page from script attacks). Payment confirmation is trusted only from signed server-side webhooks.

alternatives.why_not: comparable Indian gateway; Razorpay chosen for combined UPI + payouts + subscriptions documentation
India accounts are invite-based and UPI coverage is narrower

tradeoffs: Per-transaction fees (~2% domestic cards) are charged on revenue, not in the infrastructure band

supporting.choice: Cloudflare (free plan) in front of Azure
supporting.justification: Caches public pages and static assets near users; only public, non-personal content is cached at the edge. Azure Front Door's $35/month base fee would take 23% of the $150 budget, so the free plan is used.

alternatives.why_not: the $35/month Standard base fee is too large a share of this budget; switch when the budget grows
every asset request hits the origin; slower for distant users

tradeoffs: A second vendor for DNS/TLS, outside the Azure contract

Cloudflare positions the Free plan for projects that are not business-critical and gives it no uptime SLA (the 100% SLA starts at Business); move to a paid plan when the site becomes business-critical

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1); free minutes cover a team of 3.

alternatives.why_not: equivalent; GitHub chosen for its marketplace of deploy actions

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune)
supporting.justification: Logs and metrics stay with the host provider in Central India (Pune); alerts on error rate and latency against the 500 ms p95 target.

alternatives.why_not: stores data only in the US or EU

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.justification: Mobile users must hear about new jobs/messages immediately; FCM is no-cost and also relays to iOS via APNs. Payloads carry only an ID, never personal data.

alternatives.why_not: drains battery and misses events when the app is closed

tradeoffs: Delivery is best-effort; critical updates also appear in-app

assumptions: Hosting Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1): $25-150/month at the 'small' tier.

Database Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17: $30-120/month. Sized for Burstable B1ms (about $18 compute) to B2s (about $72 compute) plus storage; a General Purpose D2ds_v5 alone is about $183.
cdn: Cloudflare (free plan) in front of Azure $0-5/month.
observability: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune) $5-30/month.

Stored data ~50 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month: $1-3/month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average); bulk files and media are assumed to sit in object storage, while database rows stay small.
Phone OTP: 30,000 users x 0.3-1.0 OTP logins/month at India SMS ~Rs 0.20-0.25 + GST per SMS = $22-135/month (long-lived sessions keep OTPs rare).
Excluded: payment gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are a share of revenue, not infrastructure.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: DPDP Act 2023: collect consent with a clear notice, support access/correction/erasure requests, keep a breach runbook (the DPDP Rules 2025 require prompt intimation to the Board and affected people, then a detailed report within 72 hours; the Rules commence in phases, so confirm which apply on your launch date) and delete data when the purpose ends. Hosting in India simplifies transfers; legal review still required.

Upper estimate $457/month is 3.0x the $150 budget at peak usage; the largest upper-bound items are Hosting Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) (up to $150) and Phone OTP (up to $135). Launch near the $84 lower bound and set billing alerts at the budget.

assumptions: Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'small' from 30,000 users and ~800 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
